config._readme: Every tunable and every assumed number lives here, never in code. game/field values carry {value,status,source}; status is VERIFIED or TODO_VERIFY_AGAINST_MANUAL. Other sections carry _status FABRICATED (invented plausible numbers) or TUNABLE (engineering knobs). NEVER take game numbers from Chief Delphi parody documents; only the official manual counts. Schema: src/contracts/config.ts.

shotSpots._note: Named shot/staging spots relative to the hub of the acting alliance. Invented for the simulator; not field markings.

spots.description: left of the hub at medium range
right of the hub at medium range
straight back from the hub at long range
long range on the tower side

archetypes._note: Archetype templates. Every range is an invented, plausible guess, not measured from real robots. Numeric fields are [min, max]; *Probability fields are the chance a sampled team has the trait.

drum_fixed.description: Drum shooter aimed by turning the drivetrain; high volume, often tall.

turret_sotm.description: Single turret that scores while driving.

multilane_fixed.description: Two or three fixed shooting lanes aimed by the drivetrain.

big_hopper_hauler.description: Very large hopper; tall, cannot use the trench, slow when full.

dumper.description: Wide close-range dumper that must be next to the hub; fits the trench.

zero_hopper_turret.description: Almost no hopper; shoots fuel nearly as fast as it picks it up, so it needs loose or staged fuel nearby.

feeder_passer.description: Scores little; moves fuel to partners quickly by passing.

defender.description: Heavy tank drive with high push force and little or no shooter.

starter_bot.description: Simple single-lane robot with a low fire rate and a small hopper.

league._note: How the league in data/league/ is sampled from the archetype templates.

physics._note: Physics knobs for the engine. Invented defaults; P1 tunes them.

shotModel._note: Shot model knobs. Invented defaults; P1 tunes them.

triggers._note: Thresholds that turn engine conditions into decision triggers.

microRollouts._note: Short look-ahead rollouts used inside a live decision.

answerKey._note: Long rollouts that define the answer key of each scenario.

providers._note: Connection settings per provider. API keys come from .env, never from here. Models starting with TODO_ must be set by a human. drex = System 1; endpoint and auth are from console.nace.ai/docs/drex (drex-latest currently points at drex-max-v1.1; verify the model id in the console). Measured 2026-11-14 on a real 68-option play call (pnpm drex:models): drex-v2.0 evaluates in about 48 ms; drex-latest is an alias for drex-max-v1.1 and evaluates in about 150-190 ms; both chose the same option. drex-v2.0 is the default for in-match calls because latency is the headline; set model to drex-latest to compare. deepinfra = System 2 giant baseline, OpenAI-compatible chat completions; model null means: list modelsEndpoint at startup, try modelPreference in order (largest first), fall back to the next id on an access error (Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B, organizer-tested, is last), and log the exact model used in the run manifest. Ids below were in the live model list on 2026-11-14; the event key was confirmed to reach Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B. openai and gemini are optional secondary baselines.

pricesPerMTokUsd._note: US dollars per 1M tokens. byModel (exact model id) takes precedence over byId (provider fallback). null = unknown: cost is then recorded as 0, never guessed. Sources, 2026-11-14: DeepInfra models are from the pricing metadata in its live model list, and DeepInfra responses also report usage.estimated_cost, which is recorded in preference. drex-max-v1.1 is from the Nace pricing page (0.12 per 1M input tokens). drex-v2.0 at 0.06 is the price DeepInfra lists for the same model and is NOT yet confirmed against the Nace console billing page: confirm it before quoting a cost ratio. Drex bills input tokens only. openai and gemini are not filled in.

spendCapsUsd._note: Hard spend limits per run; a run aborts rather than exceed them.

realtimeLatencyCharging._note: On: the match keeps running while a provider thinks, so slow answers cost match time. Off: the match pauses.

research._note: Keenable web research, per docs.keenable.ai: POST {baseUrl}{searchPath} with { query, max_results } and GET {baseUrl}{fetchPath}?url=...; the key goes in the X-API-Key header. Both paths are confirmed with our key (2026-11-14). On 402 stop; on 429 wait Retry-After. Skip pages whose terms forbid automated access. flrstfrc.blob.core.windows.net is a lookalike of the official firstfrc host (parody documents) and is blocked.
queries: FRC 2026 REBUILT robot reveal shooter turret shoot on the move
FRC 2026 REBUILT technical binder hopper capacity drivetrain
FRC 2026 REBUILT robot trench height climb level
FRC 2026 REBUILT strategy hub shift timing active inactive
FRC 2026 REBUILT strategy defense staging passing fuel
REBUILT presented by Haas FRC 2026 game overview scoring fuel hub tower
FRC 2026 REBUILT match analysis winning alliance strategy event recap
FRC 2026 REBUILT pinning rule foul hub shift endgame tower climb points
FRC 2026 REBUILT open alliance build thread robot specifications
FRC 2020 Infinite Recharge strategy analysis cycles defense
FRC 2022 Rapid React strategy analysis cargo cycles defense

ndi._note: NDI document intelligence, per console.nace.ai/docs/ndi: POST {baseUrl}/v1/documents/{parse|split|classify|extract|ground} with Authorization: Bearer <key>; jobs are asynchronous (202 + job_id; ?wait_seconds=0..60). Same nace_sk_ key and balance as Drex. Jobs are read with GET {baseUrl}/v1/documents/jobs/{job_id}; a finished job carries cost.total_usd and cost.lines (quantity per page), which go in the usage ledger. manualUrls holds the official manual, which already includes the Team Updates (the copy fetched on 2026-11-14 is version TU22).

lab._note: Strategy Lab: Intern (github.com/nace-ai/intern) run headless as `intern -p --json --system2 <system2Provider>/<model> -- "TASK"` inside workspaceDir (the subprocess cwd). Intern 0.30.1 does not start on native Windows (it imports fcntl), so on this machine internCommand runs it inside WSL; on Linux or macOS set internCommand to the single entry intern. system2Model is the organizer-tested model; system1Model is the Drex id the organizers gave. Here the workspace lives inside WSL (workspaceDir is how Node reaches it, internCwd is the same folder as Intern sees it), where the Windows drives are not mounted, so Intern cannot reach the repo or .env. Intern is not a sandbox: the workspace holds copies only.

ledger._note: Usage ledger: one JSONL line per real external call (mock and cached calls excluded). Summarised into results/usage.json.

seeds._note: Dev seeds are for tuning; eval seeds are only for reported numbers. Never tune on eval seeds.
